Guidance now applies; lab available tomorrow. Forgo today's work. Test the new setup (1 E + W; R). Save 1 E compared with restoring the documented setup, but accept uncertainty: lab available tomorrow / lab unavailable next Sol / lab unavailable for next two Sols. Test consumes today's work even on easy outcome. Stop and ask again (0 E, no W; D). Lab unavailable today and next Sol; guidance restores it on morning Sol+2. Other base work remains possible. Learning and science: Independence versus information delay. Next-day processing includes scheduling, not light travel alone; NASA one-way range is about 4-24 minutes [9].

Diagnosis remains unknown until inspection. Move into separate shelter (0 E + W; D). Enter the persistent shelter mode defined in F10. The combined inspect-and-repair emergency action explicitly consumes W; diagnosis is revealed during it, never in the initial warning.

cds.sourceContract: E19 The Shelter Decision Prompt: The radiation monitor warns against outdoor work. You can move into the protected area, but the experiment outside will have to wait. Eligibility: Sol >=3; schedule as an adapted historical scenario, not a real-time forecast. No outdoor activity option while warning is active. Clock: missionAge for response variability only. Historical observation remains unchanged. Shelter and suspend work (1 E + W; D). Cancel today's experiment and enter the existing shielded area. No research gain; return to ordinary operation next morning in this compressed scenario. Shelter and observe remotely (3 E + W; M). Requires working robot; gain 10 / 6 / 2 D. Crew remains sheltered. Robot is occupied until next morning. Installed shielding kit reduces this option to 2 E through a simplified prepared-workspace benefit, not an electric shield. Shelter with minimum operations (0 E + W; D). Turn off nonessential equipment and pause greenhouse progress; lose 3 H as an abstract cramped-workspace/fatigue cost. Basic life support remains mandatory. No radiation damage is represented by this H cost. Source card: May 20, 2024, Curiosity RAD, Mars: reported 8,100 microgray observation [7]. This does not specify a fictional base dose or an instant health loss. Research rewards and one-Sol timing are game abstractions. A radiation monitor adds 2 D to the remote observation outcome; it does not provide shielding.
